turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response: I’m here because I can’t stop noticing this droop and unevenness around my mouth and jaw. It’s in every photo, every reflection... and even when people say I look fine, it feels really obvious to me. It’s gotten to the point where I’m avoiding presentations and meeting with clients.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient describes persistent perceived droop and unevenness of the mouth and jaw that appears obvious to them despite reassurance from others.
symptom_reasoning.S064: The patient reports avoiding presentations and meetings with clients because of the appearance concern.

turns.doctor_question: Can you describe how long this concern about the unevenness of your mouth and jaw has been bothering you, and has it affected your mood or caused you significant distress?
turns.patient_response: It’s been bothering me a lot. I can’t stop seeing the droop and unevenness around my mouth and jaw—like in every photo or reflection. Even when people tell me I look fine, it still feels really obvious to me. It’s been very upsetting, and I’ve started avoiding presentations and meeting with clients because of it.

symptom_reasoning.S067: The patient reports persistent, distressing preoccupation with perceived droop and unevenness of the mouth and jaw despite reassurance from others.
symptom_reasoning.S068: The patient describes repeatedly scrutinizing the perceived facial unevenness in every photo and reflection.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself checking your reflection, taking pictures, or doing anything repeatedly to look at or fix the area around your mouth and jaw?
turns.patient_response:
Yes. Before work or if there’s a family event, I can get stuck in the bathroom for hours checking the mirror. I take pictures on my phone from different angles to see if the droop shows, and I’ll keep redoing my makeup or adjusting a scarf to try to cover it.

I also ask my husband over and over if my face looks lopsided. And then sometimes I end up scrolling through photos of other women, comparing my face to theirs, which usually just makes me feel worse.

symptom_reasoning.S068: The patient reports hours of mirror checking, taking photos from different angles, repeatedly adjusting makeup/scarf to conceal the area, repeated reassurance seeking, and appearance comparison.
